8. SKILL.md                  # Always loaded. The checklist + constitution.
9. components/<widget>.md    # Opened on demand when the task involves that widget.

14. 
15. - **`SKILL.md`** — the rule surface. One-line principles + a link to the file that explains them. Anything a reviewer/producer should always have in working memory. Keep it tight.
16. - **`components/<widget>.md`** — widget-specific contract: Principles → Web defaults → one example → Review checklist → Pitfalls. Use when the output contains that widget.
17. - **`references/<topic>.md`** — cross-cutting web-implementation topic (contrast, focus, reflow, status messages, etc.). No Principles section — the Quick checks carry the rules; a one-paragraph intro sets context.
18. 
19. ### Naming
20. 
21. - Component filenames match the pattern name a model would reach for (`modal-dialog`, `checkbox-group`, not `dialog` or `checkboxes`).
22. - Reference filenames are the topic (`contrast-forced-colors`, `keyboard-focus`).
23.

25. 
26. Apply these when adding or editing any file in the skill:
27. 
28. 1. **Don't state the same rule twice in the same file.** Principles + Quick checks that restate each other is the most common waste. Reference files should have Quick checks only (with a short intro). Component files keep Principles because they set the widget's contract; the Review checklist should add operational detail, not repeat principles.
29. 2. **Don't state the same rule in two files.** If a rule is in a `references/*.md`, don't also expand it in `SKILL.md` link to it. If it's in `components/<widget>.md`, don't duplicate it in `references/*.md`.
30. 3. **SKILL.md web sub-bullets are a tax.** Every sub-bullet under a checklist item is loaded on every call. Keep them only when a one-line concrete instruction prevents a common mistake. Push long explanations into the referenced file.
31. 4. **One example per component.** If a minimal and an "elaborated" example both appear, collapse to the elaborated one and note what's optional. Two 20-line HTML blocks that differ by three attributes is ~600 tokens of duplication.
32. 5. **Prose lists.** Lists tokenize tighter than prose and are easier to scan. Persona/role descriptions, constraint lists, and "consider X, Y, Z" paragraphs should be bullets.
33. 6. **Cut hedges.** "Read this when reviewing", "This pattern is primarily a", "Note that" add tokens without changing output. Leading with the topic title is enough.
34. 7. **Cut obvious pitfalls.** A Pitfall that just negates a Principle from the same file ("No label on the field") is wasted. Keep pitfalls that are counterintuitive or commonly seen in model output (e.g., "Marking every checkbox `required` to express 'at least one'").

36. 9. **Don't duplicate SKILL.md rules in components.** Components should say what is *widget-specific* (focus trap in dialogs, roving tabindex in radios). Contrast, reflow, and forced-colors rules live in their reference files.
37.

39.

43. - Write the Quick checks section first. If the full file ends up saying only what the Quick checks say, delete the rest.
44. 
45. ## When editing an existing file
46. 
47. - Re-read the file's Quick checks (or Review checklist) first. If your addition is already covered there, rephrase the existing item instead of adding a new one.
48. - If you find a rule duplicated across two files, pick the file where it primarily belongs, delete the other copy, and add a link.

50.

52. 
53. Rough targets (not hard limits). A file materially larger than this usually has duplication:
54. 
55. - `SKILL.md`: under ~250 lines.
56. - `components/<widget>.md`: under ~120 lines.
57. - `references/<topic>.md`: under ~80 lines (testing.md is the exception because it documents runtime probing).

64. - [ ] Each component file has at most one HTML example.
65. - [ ] New component added to `components/README.md`.
66. - [ ] Pitfalls list contains only counterintuitive/common mistakes, not negations of Principles.

 3. **SKILL.md web sub-bullets are a tax.** Every sub-bullet under a checklist item is loaded on every call. Keep them only when a one-line concrete instruction prevents a common mistake. Push long explanations into the referenced file.
 4. **One example per component.** If a minimal and an "elaborated" example both appear, collapse to the elaborated one and note what's optional. Two 20-line HTML blocks that differ by three attributes is ~600 tokens of duplication.
 5. **Prose lists.** Lists tokenize tighter than prose and are easier to scan. Persona/role descriptions, constraint lists, and "consider X, Y, Z" paragraphs should be bullets.
 6. **Cut hedges.** "Read this when reviewing", "This pattern is primarily a", "Note that" add tokens without changing output. Leading with the topic title is enough.
